The native engine guide

Source: vignettes/articles/native-guide.qmd

The native engine fits models from lavaan-style syntax by maximum likelihood, with a covariance structure and, when you write intercepts, observed means. This guide covers the whole workflow in one place: syntax, fitting, inference, constraints, model comparison, diagnostics and the route to the mediation objects. For a first look, read the five-minute quickstart.

Entry points fit_sem(syntax, data); fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native") for one mediator
Class returned SEMFit, then MediationData, SerialMediationData or ParallelMediationData from extract_mediation()
Syntax reference ?"medfit-syntax"
Not covered latent means, latent products, groups, categorical outcomes, other estimators; see the limits 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
d <- mediation_demo

1. Syntax

Statement Meaning
y ~ x1 + x2 regression of y on x1 and x2
f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 latent variable f measured by indicators
y1 ~~ y2 covariance; y1 ~~ y1 is a variance
y ~ a*x label a path; equal labels are one parameter
y ~ 0.5*x fix a path
start(0.3)*, lower(0)*, upper(1)* starting value, lower and upper bound
ab := a*b defined parameter with a delta-method standard error
a == b, cp == a*b, a*b > 0.1 equality or inequality constraint on labels, linear or not
y1, y2 ~ x comma shorthand (a medfit extension; lavaan reads it differently)

Exogenous observed variables are fixed at their sample moments by default, as lavaan does with fixed.x = TRUE (fewer parameters, the same structural estimates, a conditional log likelihood); fixed_x = FALSE in fit_sem() gives them free variances and covariances instead. Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition are arithmetic expressions in the labels (+ - * / ^, parentheses, exp, log, sqrt, abs, min, max, pnorm, qnorm, and a few more).

2. Fit and read 

syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
"
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, d)
summary(fit)

The chi-square is \(n\) times the minimized discrepancy and has df degrees of freedom. A saturated model (here df = 0) fits perfectly by construction, so the test only means something when there are restrictions.

3. Standard errors and weights

The default information matrix is observed; information = "expected" gives lavaan’s default. se_type = "sandwich" gives the HC0 robust covariance, and weights takes case weights.

w <- seq_len(nrow(d)) %% 3 + 1
robust <- fit_sem(syntax, d, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
rbind(model_based = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))[1:3], weighted_robust = sqrt(diag(vcov(robust)))[1:3])
                         a mediator1~covariate1          b
model_based     0.09858458           0.04833820 0.05306479
weighted_robust 0.10207525           0.04774111 0.06498487

4. Constraints

A constraint is a line of syntax. The engine classifies it and uses the cheapest exact route:

Constraint Example How it is solved
linear equality or bound a == b, a + b == 1, a < 0.3 constant Jacobian rows; every accepted solution passes a gate on all rows
nonlinear equality cp == a*b Jacobian recomputed at every point; every start tried, the best accepted one kept; a Newton polish after acceptance
nonlinear inequality a*b > 0.1, ab > 0 with ab := a*b same, as rows \(c(\theta) \le 0\); a warning when the starts disagree
one independent nonzero product a*b == 0.1 both sign domains searched; an unresolved required branch stops the fit; coverage is not global optimality
product set to zero a*b == 0, b1*b2*b3 == 0 exact: one linear fit per factor, smallest discrepancy kept
sum of products a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0 best-effort: the best of the starts; a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, so raise n_starts 
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), d)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
     a      b     cp
0.5423 0.5497 0.2981 
tied@diagnostics$active_constraints
[1] "cp == a * b"

Labels used in a constraint must be defined in the model, and a constraint with no free parameter is an error. CONSTRAINT(a == b) is the same as the bare a == b.

5. Compare models and test the indirect effect

anova() is the likelihood-ratio test for nested SEMFits; it refits nothing. Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion, a necessary condition, so two models that pass but are not nested in substance are your responsibility. mbco_sem() tests an indirect effect that is a product of paths:

anova(tied, fit)
Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models

n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy

     Df Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit   0 0.000
tied  1 0.938    0.93802       1     0.3328
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * b = 0
MBCO = 33.353, df = 1, p-value = 7.685e-09

For a chain a, d, b, give the paths: mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b")) is the minimum of the single-path tests against a chi-square with one degree of freedom. The null is a union of hypotheses, so the test is conservative when more than one path is zero (its size is at most 0.055 at the 5% level in the package’s simulation gate).

6. Diagnostics

Read these before trusting a fit; all are in summary(fit) and fit@diagnostics:

Field What it says If it is wrong
Converged the optimizer returned and the acceptance gate passed the fit is not returned; the error names the failure
Optimizer status, stationarity the solver’s code and the Newton decrement at the solution a large decrement means a stall; try n_starts
Active bounds / Active constraints which bounds or constraints bind a binding bound means the estimate is on the edge
Improper solution a negative variance or non-positive definite covariance respecify, or bound the variance
Multiplier sign check active inequality multipliers have the right sign a wrong sign means an active bound was not optimal 
b <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome\n"), d)
b@diagnostics$active_bounds
[1] "outcome~~outcome"

For the nonzero-product supported shapes, local-search limits and coverage record, see the constraints page.

When a model with a nonlinear constraint warns that the starts reached different optima, the constraint has more than one solution (a*b > 0.1 holds for two positive or two negative paths). The kept fit is the best, but say so in a report.

The outcome ledger

Every native fit keeps a versioned record of how it was reached, fit@diagnostics$ledger: one node per fit, zero-product branch and mbco_sem() null, each with its optimizer state, likelihood, covariance status and notices. A node is resolved (the optimizer accepted it) or unresolved, and unresolved means unknown: only a feasibility of certified_empty is a proof that a branch has no solution, and only a literal contradiction such as a == 0 with a == 1 earns it. Errors that stop a fit carry the same ledger as $ledger, and mbco_sem() and compare_lr() return it with an unresolved result. Read it with str(fit@diagnostics$ledger, max.level = 2); the cases and what to do are in Troubleshooting, and the construction is in Computation and algorithms.

7. From a fit to mediation objects 

x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
class(x)[1]
[1] "medfit::MediationData"

fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native", treatment =, mediator =) does both steps for one mediator. For several mediators, fit with fit_sem() and call extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c("m1", "m2"), outcome = ): a chain gives a SerialMediationData, mediators side by side a ParallelMediationData. A latent mediator works through the same call.

Limits

  • Observed means only. Intercepts (y ~ 1, y ~ 1 + x) are estimated for observed variables; a free latent mean or intercept stops with “latent means are planned for a later release”.
  • One group; listwise deletion is the missing-data default. The separate bounded FIML opt-in retains partially observed rows only for its three-variable random-X model.
  • ML only, plus the HC0 sandwich; no robust chi-square, no fit indices beyond the chi-square, AIC and BIC.
  • Products (x:m, which give the four-way decomposition) work for two observed variables inside a supported class; the table of limits and messages is on the native model page. The model test is NA when a product factor is a regression target.
  • AIC and BIC of a fit with a product are not comparable with those of a fit without one (the product column enters the likelihood), so AIC(fit_a, fit_b) and BIC() refuse such a pair; see the native model page.
  • For latent means, groups, categorical outcomes or fit indices use lavaan; the extraction route accepts a lavaan fit as well. See lavaan and the native engine.

Bounded FIML (0.16.0)

Bounded FIML was introduced in 0.16.0 and is unavailable in released 0.15.0. Ordinary calls still delete incomplete model rows listwise. The explicit opt-in below fits exactly three numeric continuous observed variables: X to M to Y with a free or exactly zero direct path, independent Gaussian disturbances and free intercepts. It assumes ignorable missingness under that joint model; FIML does not impute the missing values.

Generate continuous Gaussian X, M and Y with independent disturbances for this example; the bundled demo’s binary treatment does not match this joint model. The fixed missing-value pattern is for illustration, not evidence that missingness in an applied study is ignorable. with_seed() preserves the caller’s random-number state.

fiml_data <- withr::with_seed(271L, {
  n <- 400L
  treatment <- .8 + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 1.1)
  mediator1 <- -.4 + .5 * treatment + stats::rnorm(n, sd = .8)
  outcome <- .7 + .6 * mediator1 + .25 * treatment + stats::rnorm(n, sd = .9)
  data.frame(treatment = treatment, mediator1 = mediator1, outcome = outcome)
})
fiml_data$mediator1[seq(1, nrow(fiml_data), by = 7)] <- NA_real_
fiml_syntax <- "mediator1 ~ a*treatment
outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment"
fiml_fit <- medfit::fit_sem(
  fiml_syntax, fiml_data, missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE,
  meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed", se_type = "model"
)
c(retained_rows = nobs(fiml_fit), logLik = as.numeric(logLik(fiml_fit)))
retained_rows        logLik
      400.000     -1544.246 
fiml_effects <- extract_mediation(fiml_fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
nie(fiml_effects)
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2795
nde(fiml_effects)
Natural Direct Effect (NDE): 0.2474
te(fiml_effects)
Total Effect (TE): 0.5269
tidy(fiml_effects, type = "effects")
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  term  estimate std_error
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.279    0.0365
2 nde      0.247    0.0508
3 te       0.527    0.0457

The wrapper route returns the extracted mediation object directly:

fiml_wrapped <- medfit::fit_mediation(
  model = fiml_syntax, data = fiml_data,
  treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1", engine = "native",
  se_type = "model", engine_args = list(
    missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE, information = "observed"
  )
)
tidy(fiml_wrapped, type = "effects")
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  term  estimate std_error
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.279    0.0365
2 nde      0.247    0.0508
3 te       0.527    0.0457

There is no new top-level missing argument on fit_mediation(); med() remains a formula-building fitter. The missing-method strings must match exactly. A failed FIML fit never falls back to listwise deletion or another engine, even on complete data.

Setting Bounded FIML requirement
fixed_x Explicit FALSE; omission, TRUE and named subsets refuse
meanstructure TRUE; NULL and FALSE refuse
information, se_type "observed", "model"
Weights No non-NULL vector, including unit weights or the deprecated alias
n_starts, control NULL or 3; empty control; no syntax-supplied starts
Topology Three variables only; free or exactly zero direct path; no :=, constraints, ties, bounds, extra predictors, latent variables, factors or products

The start/control restrictions preserve the initial validated protocol, rather than expressing mathematical limits of FIML. Three starts run for each solver; six attempt groups normally involve nine actual calls with nlminb refinements. Failures and completed calls are retained separately. Numerical acceptance requires both solvers, stationarity, agreeing likelihoods, local rank and valid observed information; it does not certify a global optimum or inference coverage.

Rows with any observed model variable are retained, including singleton patterns; only all-empty model rows are dropped. Extra columns do not select rows. No complete-case initialization is used: data with no complete rows can fit when local identification checks pass. nobs() counts retained rows, not observed cells. Original positional row IDs and pattern/count evidence are retained.

coef(), full vcov(), nobs(), raw logLik(), AIC/BIC, print/summary, parameter tidy and normal confidence intervals work on the SEMFit. Its glance() reports likelihood/IC fields, with model-test fields unavailable and an explicit reason. The discrepancy f and model-test df are NA; the separate free-parameter count is eight or nine. There is no saturated missing-data fit. See Methods and Formulas for the likelihood.

Extraction preserves validated FIML context through copying and serialization. Original SEMFit labels/full covariance stay unchanged; extracted a/b/c_prime and m_/y_ aliases follow topology, with original coordinates retained in context. Supported extracted operations are paths(), nie(), nde(), te(), coef() (paths/effects/all), full vcov(), print/summary, tidy and normal path/effect confidence intervals. At a = b = 0 the NIE point value is retained but its inferential fields are unavailable. A fixed direct path of zero instead has known zero covariance; other valid effect inference remains available.

Extracted-object glance(), quick(), pm(), bootstrap/boot intervals, profiles, MBCO, fit tests, fit indices and prediction/residual APIs are deferred and refuse FIML objects. Package object-aware guards act before package-controlled refits, RNG or worker launch; opaque user callbacks are outside this guarantee. AIC/BIC comparisons dispatched with SEMFit first require compatible FIML contexts and refuse external/mixed objects before external likelihood calls. Calls dispatched first through another class are outside medfit’s guard.
